chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He (the Imam) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not create anything in the sky without having an equivalent for it in the earth, and He did not create anything in the earth without having an equivalent for it in the sky. So when a righteous man from the people of the earth dies, Allah raises up for him something in the sky which is called: a righteous star. And when a wretched man from the people of the sky dies, Allah casts him down to the earth.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between righteous people on earth and stars in the sky according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to elucidate the concept of *al-mathal al-a'la* (the highest archetype), illustrating how the terrestrial world mirrors the celestial spheres through divine symmetry. This hadith underscores the Shia belief in a structured, interconnected cosmos where spiritual status on earth is reflected in the heavens, reinforcing the idea that creation is a unified, hierarchical manifestation of God's will.
